verdict.rationale: TypeSafe publishes model-level transparency material for its flagship jev-1.13: a limitations page covering nine known failure modes with mitigations, and a models page with versioning, context limits and data-handling statements. These cover part of what a model card would hold, but nothing in the pack is a formal model or system card. Missing for 10: a consolidated model/system card, documented training approach (only 'not trained on customer requests' and 'same weights serve every account'), published evaluation/benchmark results for the model, an explicit intended-use statement, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can read a published model card or system card — capabilities, training approach, evaluation results, and intended use — for the current flagship model

citations.quote: Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of with jev-1.13
Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses.
Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data... the same weights serve every account.
